scope_note.intro: This score only measures the technical and on-page hygiene of your site: is it set up correctly, is anything in the way. On its own it does not tell whether the site will show up in search. Not measured:
items: Indexing status: whether Google has actually indexed the page
Rankings and the searches you appear in
Backlinks (links from other sites) and authority
Field speed data: what real users experience (the speed measurement below is a lab value taken from this machine)
scope_note.model_note: The score is an estimated model: the weights are this product's internal model and have not been calibrated against real rankings.
scope_note.next_step: What can be done: connect your Google account (Search Console) for indexing and search data; only read access is requested; until it is connected, the Visibility signals below are informational only.
scope_note.title: What this score does not measure

checks.message: The H1 heading is not visible in the first screen (above the fold) on desktop or mobile.
The canonical names a different URL, so this page asks search engines to index that URL instead. Confirm this is intended.
The Content-Type response header and the meta tag declare different character encodings.
Neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive limits framing of the page.
One or more cookies are set without the Secure flag.
csp
The DOM is nested more than 32 levels deep, which slows rendering (Lighthouse guidance).
The page uses HTML tags that are obsolete, such as <center> or <font>.
No favicon is declared and /favicon.ico does not exist.
Hreflang and canonical disagree: the page or a target names a different canonical URL than the one used in the hreflang set.
The same language code points at two different URLs in one hreflang set.
A hreflang value is not a valid language or language-region code (for example 'eng', 'jp' or 'en-uk').
The page's own hreflang language differs from its <html lang> attribute.
The page has hreflang links but none of them points to the page itself. Hreflang sets should include a self reference.
A page points to a language version that does not point back. Search engines ignore an unreciprocated hreflang pair.
The hreflang set has several languages but no x-default entry for visitors whose language is not listed.
A hreflang target is marked noindex, so it cannot be shown as the language version.
A hreflang target does not answer 200 directly (error, unreachable or it redirects).
hsts
The HTML response is larger than 1.5 KB and is sent without compression (no Content-Encoding).
The HTML is larger than 2 MB. Googlebot reads only the first 2 MB of an HTML file, measured before compression, so content after that point is not considered for indexing.
https-redirect
The home page is also reachable at /index.html or /index.php with a 200 and no canonical.
A fixed layer (cookie banner, dialog or pop-up) covers more than 30% of the first screen.
This HTTPS page links to plain http:// addresses.
The web app manifest linked from the page cannot be fetched or is not valid JSON.
The page redirects with a meta refresh. Google follows it, but a server side 301 or 308 redirect is the more reliable choice.
The page has no canonical link. Search engines then choose the preferred URL themselves.
No character encoding is declared for the document.
The document does not start with <!doctype html>, so browsers fall back to quirks mode.
This HTTPS page loads resources over plain HTTP. Browsers block or warn about these.
The HTML response has neither ETag nor Last-Modified, so clients cannot revalidate it cheaply (heuristic).
The 404 response looks like a bare server default page without navigation (heuristic).
The page asks search engines not to follow any of its links. Confirm this is intended.
A robots meta tag asks search engines not to index this page. Confirm this is intended.
The X-Robots-Tag response header asks search engines not to index this page. Confirm this is intended.
X-Content-Type-Options is not set to nosniff.
A sampled page answers with a 4xx status (not found or blocked).
A sampled page answers with a 5xx server error.
The URL redirects through two or more hops before the final page. This is a heuristic, not a search engine limit.
The Referrer-Policy is unsafe-url or not a recognised value.
robots
The server took more than 1.8 seconds to start answering from this measurement point. The figure depends on where it was measured; it is a heuristic.
A URL that does not exist answers with 200 (or redirects to a 200 page) instead of 404.
tls
The same page answers with 200 both with and without a trailing slash and no canonical separates them.
The page is also reachable with an upper-case path and both answer with 200.
The page uses frames. Content inside frames is hard for search engines to attribute to this URL.
One element has more than 60 direct children, which is slow to lay out (Lighthouse guidance).
The www and non-www hosts end on different URLs.
Some links in the content use generic text such as "click here", which says nothing about where they lead.
Heading levels skip inside the main content, for example from H2 to H4. Google Search does not mind heading order, but screen reader users move through a page by heading level.
Some links have no accessible text: no link text, no label and no image alt text.
The meta description is longer than 160 characters and may be truncated in results. This is a display heuristic, not a published search engine limit.
No H1 heading was found on the page.
The html element does not declare the page language with a lang attribute.
The page has no meta description. Search engines write their own snippet when none is given.
The page has no og:image, so shared links show no preview image.
The page has neither og:title nor og:image, so shared links show no title or preview image.
The page has no title tag. Search engines then build the result title from other text, such as the main heading.
The page has no viewport meta tag, so phones render it zoomed out.
The page has more than one H1. Google says there is no ideal number of headings, so this does not affect Search on its own. Check that the most prominent heading names the page.
The og:image is a relative URL. Most social crawlers need an absolute URL (https://...).
The og:image is smaller than 1200x630 pixels; large cards may be shown small or cropped.
The og:image URL does not return an image (error, missing file or unreachable). Social networks will show no picture.
The og:image does not have the usual 1.91:1 ratio; platforms may crop it.
og:url differs from the canonical, so social shares may point at a different URL than search engines use.
The title is longer than 60 characters and may be truncated in results. This is a display heuristic, not a published search engine limit.
The title is shorter than 30 characters. A very short title rarely describes the page well enough to earn a click. This is a heuristic, not a search engine rule.
There is no twitter:card tag. X/Twitter falls back to Open Graph but shows a small card by default.
The URL path has a double slash, which often creates accidental duplicate URLs.
The URL has query parameters other than tracking parameters. Parameters can create duplicate versions of the same page.
The URL has unencoded non-ASCII characters. Words in the audience's language are fine in URLs; links should use the percent encoded form so the address survives copying.
The URL is longer than 100 characters. Long URLs are harder to share and may be truncated in results. This is a heuristic, not a search engine limit.
The URL path uses underscores. Hyphens are the usual word separator in URLs.
The URL path has uppercase letters. URLs are case sensitive, so mixed case invites duplicates and broken links.
The page links to an external URL that answers with an error or cannot be reached. This can be temporary.
The page links to an internal URL that answers with an error (for example 404) or cannot be reached.
An internal link points to a URL that redirects before reaching the page.
At least a fifth of the page's internal links carry rel=nofollow. This is a heuristic.
Several links with visible text point nowhere (href="#" or javascript:void). Visitors and crawlers cannot follow them. This is a heuristic: a link may be wired to a script.
The page has more than 150 links. This is a heuristic, not a limit set by search engines.
A target keyword you gave does not appear in the meta description.
A target keyword you gave does not appear in the H1 heading.
A target keyword you gave does not appear in the title tag.
A target keyword makes up more than 3% of the words. Google publishes no density rule; this is a readability warning.
More than 30% of the sentences are longer than 25 words.
Placeholder text such as lorem ipsum was found in the visible content.
The text is very difficult to read by the Flesch / Atesman score (long sentences and long words).
The page has fewer than 200 words of visible body text. Google has no minimum word count, so this is not a ranking rule. Check that the page fully answers what a visitor came for.
Some buttons, form fields or links have no accessible name, so an agent (or a screen reader) cannot tell what they do.
robots.txt blocks at least one AI search crawler at the site root.
A large share of the page content only exists after JavaScript runs. Many AI crawlers do not run JavaScript (heuristic).
The site's /llms.txt exists but does not follow the llmstxt.org proposal (title, summary, sections with links). Google Search ignores this file.
